newsitem.title: FINLAND: UNION, EMPLOYER EMU BUFFER VIEWS CLOSER - LIPPONEN.
newsitem.headline: UNION, EMPLOYER EMU BUFFER VIEWS CLOSER - LIPPONEN.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Wednesday that the views of trade unions and employer confederations on so called buffer for European economic and monetary union (EMU) had moved closer.

"This morning's discussions showed that different views on what the so called buffer funds actually mean have moved closer to each other," Lipponen told Reuters after a meeting of the economic council -- a discussion forum grouping key cabinet ministers, the central bank governor and leaders of the labour market organisations and other big industry and business lobbies.
The economic council on Wednesday morning discussed a report on the impact of potential asymmetric shocks on the Finnish economy in the single currency environment.
The report would not be made public.

"The labour market groups and other organisations see that the most important factors are economic factors such as moderate inflation, cost control and an overall stable economic development," Lipponen said.

Director-general Johannes Koroma of the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) said on Monday at an EMU seminar arranged by the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) that TT was willing to talk with unions about buffer funds for EMU.
SAK said that the labour market organisations should come to terms on the buffer funds at the latest in the autumn.
